stories.title: BXP Sells D.C. Office to Jemal Equities for $92M
stories.excerpt: BXP has unloaded a 254,000-square-foot office building in Washington, D.C.’s Dupont Circle for $92.3 million as the firm sheds older properties in the nation’s capital. Affiliates of Jemal Equities acquired the building at 1330 Connecticut Avenue NW, according to deed records cited by the Business Journals. Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust provided $72.5 million in financing for the deal. Douglas Development Managing Principal Matthew Jemal runs Jemal Equities. The acquisition is the company’s fourth D.C. office purchase in about 14 months in deals totaling almost $227 million. In May, the firm acquired a 235,000-square-foot office building at 99 M Street SE for $93.2 million from an affiliate of Polinger. A month earlier, it purchased the 155,000-square-foot Lion Building at 1233 20th Street NW from affiliates of MRP Realty and BGO for $12.4 million. Jemal Equities also acquired the 123,000-square-foot property at 1750 H Street NW for $28.8 million last year. For BXP, the disposition is part of a broader strategy to sell older D.C. office assets while directing capital toward new trophy office developments. The Boston-based real estate investment trust is developing projects at 725 12th Street NW and 2100 M Street NW, both pre-leased to law firms. The properties represent the only new private office construction in D.C.’s pipeline. The company also transferred its leasehold interest in the 210,000-square-foot Sumner Square office complex to an affiliate of Vieron Capital for $63 million in August. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BXP sells 254K SF D.C. office at 1330 Connecticut Ave NW for $92.3M to Jemal Equities.
Jemal Equities acquired four D.C. office buildings totaling ~$227M in 14 months; Burke & Herbert financed $72.5M.
BXP divesting older D.C. office stock; Jemal positioning as distressed office buyer in Dupont Circle submarket.
stories.summary: BXP divested a 254,000-square-foot office building in Washington, D.C.'s Dupont Circle to Jemal Equities for $92.3 million, with $72.5 million in financing from Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust. Jemal Equities has acquired four D.C. office properties totaling approximately $227 million over the past 14 months, signaling aggressive accumulation of distressed or discounted older office assets. The transaction reflects BXP's broader retreat from legacy D.C. office holdings and a buyer-of-last-resort dynamic in the nation's capital's office market.
stories.impact: BXP's exit from aging D.C. office and Jemal's four-property spree signals persistent supply-side pressure and capitulation pricing in Washington D.C.'s office sector; multifamily developers should monitor whether Jemal converts these assets to residential or mixed-use, which could signal emerging adaptive-reuse opportunities. The weakness in D.C. office (despite federal presence) underscores that government employment stability does not insulate metros from broader office-to-residential conversion trends.

stories.title: Seattle-Based Avatar Financial Group Provides Financing for OH Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Avatar Financial Group has provided a $3.045 million bridge loan secured by a neighborhood retail center in suburban Cleveland, Ohio. The 18-month, first-lien loan was originated at 64% loan-to-value. The sponsors required an expedited closing to acquire the property after traditional lenders proved unable to meet the transaction’s timetable. They own a significant portfolio of stable commercial real estate assets. The loan’s 18-month term gives the sponsors time to lease the center’s remaining space and build the operating history that a conventional lender will want for a fully occupied property before refinancing. Located at 26508-26520 Lorain Road in North Olmsted, the two-building property contains approximately 67,450 square feet on 6.83 acres. The main center was built in 1979 and renovated in 2001, and a 4,500-square-foot outlot building was completed in 2002. Ashley Furniture Outlet anchors the center, and Vitamin Shoppe occupies the outlot building. Nearby retailers include Giant Eagle, Marc’s Stores and The Home Depot. bullets: Avatar Financial Group provides $3.045M bridge loan at 64% LTV for retail center in North Olmsted, Ohio.

stories.summary: Avatar Financial Group originated an $3.045 million, 18-month first-lien bridge loan at 64% LTV for a 67,450-square-foot neighborhood retail center at 26508-26520 Lorain Road in North Olmsted, Ohio. The sponsors required expedited closing after traditional lenders could not meet the acquisition timeline. The loan's term is sized to allow the sponsors to lease remaining space and build operating history needed for conventional refinance.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily. This reflects broader tightening of traditional construction and acquisition lending timelines, which indirectly signals stress in real estate lending generally and higher cost of capital for faster closings—a factor that can reduce competition for multifamily sites and push some developers toward bridge structures.

stories.title: Insights from Connect Apartments: Finding Opportunities in Challenges (VIDEO)
stories.excerpt: At Connect Apartments 2026 in Los Angeles, Connect CRE asked industry leaders where they’re seeing trends, opportunities or challenges in the Western multifamily market. While not downplaying the challenges that have arisen in an uncertain financing environment, these experts highlighted the opportunities that result from paying attention to fundamental operating principles and having a strong team in place. “We see a tremendous opportunity in this next three or four years as assets come to market at reasonable prices, even attractive prices,” said Ethan Penner, chairman of Hill Street Realty, who was interviewed by Connect Media president and CEO Daniel Ceniceros at the outset of the in-person industry event. “Fortunes are typically made in this time, and we hope to be one of the beneficiaries.” In the video below, you’ll also hear from Lonnie Hendry, chief product officer with Trepp; Amit Tyagi, principal with Gantry; Ivan Viramontes, associate director, Talonvest Capital; and Michael Cohen, managing partner, Brighton Capital Advisors. The post Insights from Connect Apartments: Finding Opportunities in Challenges (VIDEO) appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Connect Apartments 2026 L.A. event features industry leaders on Western multifamily market trends and opportunities.
Ethan Penner (Hill Street Realty) cites "tremendous opportunity in next 3–4 years" as assets come to market at "reasonable, even attractive prices."
Experts highlight strong fundamentals and team quality as keys to capturing value in uncertain financing environment.
stories.summary: At Connect Apartments 2026 in Los Angeles, multifamily industry leaders including Ethan Penner (Hill Street Realty), Lonnie Hendry (Trepp), Amit Tyagi (Gantry), Ivan Viramontes (Talonvest Capital), and Michael Cohen (Brighton Capital Advisors) discussed trends and opportunities in Western multifamily. Penner specifically highlighted a 3–4 year window in which assets are expected to reach reasonable and attractive pricing, positioning it as a wealth-creation opportunity for well-capitalized, operationally disciplined investors.
stories.impact: Signals consensus among top Western multifamily operators that the market has entered or is entering a buyer's window—asset prices are likely stabilizing or declining, and distressed/non-performing portfolios and mezzanine debt may be coming to market soon. Developers with capital and acquisition acumen should prepare to move quickly on off-market or lender-forced sales, particularly in L.A., which has inventory pressure and finite land.

stories.title: Greystone Provides $35M in Freddie Mac Financing for Naperville Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Greystone has provided a $35.37 million Freddie Mac loan to finance the acquisition of The Ponds of Naperville, a 216-unit multifamily property in Naperville, Illinois. The financing was originated by Eric Rosenstock, Senior Managing Director at Greystone on behalf of Grand Lifestyles. Built in 1988, The Ponds of Naperville offers a mix of one- and two-bedroom apartments. A total of 164 units have previously been renovated with features including stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, gray cabinetry and vinyl flooring. “The acquisition market in suburban Illinois is particularly exciting given that it remains one of the few markets experiencing organic rent growth, driven in large part by a lack of new supply and strong underlying multifamily fundamentals,” said Rosenstock. “The Ponds of Naperville presented Grand Lifestyles with an opportunity to acquire a well-maintained community in an established Chicago-area submarket, and we were pleased to once again work with their team to provide financing that supports the continued growth of their multifamily portfolio.” The post Greystone Provides $35M in Freddie Mac Financing for Naperville Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystone closes $35.37M Freddie Mac financing for 216-unit The Ponds of Naperville acquisition; built 1988, 164 units renovated.
Grand Lifestyles buyer; Eric Rosenstock (Greystone) cites "organic rent growth" and "lack of new supply" in suburban Illinois.
Naperville and suburban Chicago remain acquisition target due to limited new multifamily deliveries and strong fundamentals.
stories.summary: Greystone provided a $35.37 million Freddie Mac loan to Grand Lifestyles for the acquisition of The Ponds of Naperville, a 216-unit multifamily property built in 1988 with 164 units recently renovated. Greystone's Eric Rosenstock cited organic rent growth in suburban Illinois driven by a lack of new supply and strong multifamily fundamentals. The deal underscores the attractiveness of well-maintained, stabilized communities in established Chicago-area submarkets.
stories.impact: Naperville and suburban Illinois are experiencing organic rent growth precisely because new supply is constrained—developers looking to compete must identify submarkets with similar constraints (low permitting/zoning barriers, limited buildable land, or slow entitlements) where infill or value-add plays can capture rental tailwinds. This financing at Freddie Mac terms indicates strong asset fundamentals and low refinance risk, signaling stable yield for later-stage acquisitions or hold strategies.

stories.title: DC Retail Investment Activity Increases, Virginia Suburbs Show Strength
stories.excerpt: Across the Washington, D.C., area, more retail space was leased than vacated in 2025, despite federal government layoffs and broader economic headwinds, according to a recent report by Marcus & Millichap. The metro recorded a roughly 30 percent year-over-year increase in retail transaction activity, slightly outpacing the national rate. “Washington-area retail properties have remained resilient despite ongoing labor market pressures,” said Brian Hosey, senior managing director, market leader. “Improving office fundamentals and steady conditions in Northern Virginia are helping support retail demand.” Northern Virginia’s retail submarkets held vacancy steady as of June while the District and Maryland suburbs recorded year-over-year vacancy increases. Retail transaction activity tripled in the Dulles Corridor and nearly doubled in the Alexandria/Interstate 395 area and Southeast Fairfax County. “Investor activity has strengthened across the metro, with Northern Virginia posting some of the largest gains in transaction volume,” added Hosey. The post DC Retail Investment Activity Increases, Virginia Suburbs Show Strength appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: D.C. area retail more space leased than vacated in 2025; 30% YoY increase in transaction activity despite federal layoffs.
Northern Virginia retail vacancy held steady; D.C. District and Maryland suburbs saw YoY vacancy increases; Dulles Corridor and Alexandria transaction activity tripled/nearly doubled.
Northern Virginia posting largest transaction gains; office fundamentals and steady conditions supporting retail demand per Marcus & Millichap.
stories.summary: The Washington, D.C., metro area recorded a 30 percent year-over-year increase in retail transaction activity in 2025, with more space leased than vacated despite federal government layoffs. Northern Virginia held retail vacancy steady while D.C. District and Maryland suburbs posted vacancy increases. Transaction activity tripled in the Dulles Corridor and nearly doubled in Alexandria/I-395 and Southeast Fairfax County, with Northern Virginia posting the largest investor activity gains.
stories.impact: Northern Virginia retail strength signals job and population resilience in that submarket—likely driven by private-sector and defense/federal contractor activity less sensitive to government headcount cuts. For multifamily developers, this is a leading indicator of continued rental demand in Northern Virginia metros (Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun corridors), especially near retail-anchored nodes; D.C. proper retail weakness may presage continued apartment supply pressure and softer rents in core urban D.C. unless office-to-residential conversions accelerate.

stories.title: Genentech Breaks Ground on $750M Manufacturing Expansion in Hillsboro
stories.excerpt: Genentech, a subsidiary of Swiss drugmaker Roche Group, has broken ground on a $750 million expansion of its manufacturing facility in Hillsboro, Oregon. The move advances plans announced in August to increase capacity for advanced drug delivery devices and to strengthen the company’s United States manufacturing capabilities. The event marks the start of construction for the 211,000-square-foot expansion, doubling the size of the existing site. Commercial operations are planned to begin in 2031. The expansion will create approximately 250 manufacturing jobs. Genentech established its Hillsboro campus in 2006. Today, the 75-acre campus is an important part of the company’s manufacturing network, with capabilities spanning drug product manufacturing, packaging, distribution and individualized therapies. “As construction begins we are one step closer to bringing device fill-finish manufacturing to Hillsboro, strengthening our domestic supply chain and investing in the people and infrastructure that will help us deliver the medicines of the future,” said Genentech CEO Ashley Magargee. The post Genentech Breaks Ground on $750M Manufacturing Expansion in Hillsboro appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Genentech (Roche subsidiary) breaks ground on $750M expansion; 211K SF doubles Hillsboro, Oregon campus; commercial ops begin 2031.
Expansion creates ~250 manufacturing jobs; strengthens U.S. supply chain for advanced drug delivery and individualized therapies.
75-acre campus established 2006; major long-cycle capital commitment signals durable employer presence and in-migration potential.
stories.summary: Genentech, a Roche subsidiary, broke ground on a $750 million, 211,000-square-foot manufacturing facility expansion in Hillsboro, Oregon, doubling the size of its existing 75-acre campus. The expansion will create approximately 250 manufacturing jobs and begin commercial operations in 2031. The move is part of a broader strategy to strengthen U.S. manufacturing capabilities for advanced drug delivery devices.
stories.impact: Genentech's $750M long-cycle capex in Hillsboro signals durable job creation (250 roles) and employer commitment through 2031+, driving labor-force in-migration to the Portland metro and nearby communities. Multifamily developers should target Hillsboro, Beaverton, and Lake Oswego submarkets for acquisition/development pipelines; this manufacturing anchor will attract mid-to-senior technical talent requiring housing. The 2031 completion timeline means apartment demand will ramp 2027–2031, favoring near-term site control and entitlements in walkable, transit-accessible nodes near the campus.

stories.title: Educational Nonprofit Signs Lease to Build Campus on Brooklyn’s Floyd Bennett Field
stories.excerpt: The National Park Service has leased a 7-acre space in Brooklyn’s Marine Park neighborhood to a workforce development nonprofit. Runway Green signed a 60-year agreement with the federal government to build a $60 million agricultural and environmental education facility at Floyd Bennett Field, according to the organization. The former airfield near Jamaica Bay is within Gateway National Recreation Area, which the Park Service oversees. The first phase of the project will break ground next year when 3 acres will be dedicated to urban farming in partnership with the Campaign Against Hunger. “This lease turns a bold vision into a public commitment to New York City’s young people,” Geoff Roehm, founder and executive director of Runway Green, said in a statement. “At Floyd Bennett Field, we will build an educational ecosystem where schools, employers, nonprofits, colleges and public agencies work together to create learning experiences no single institution could provide on its own.” A rendering of Runway Green’s proposed education campus at Floyd Bennett Field, Brooklyn. RENDERING: Courtesy ARO, SCAPE, Colloqate Runway Green has already raised $9.3 million toward its $60 million budget from a mix of government sources, such as $1 million from Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso, $3.3 million from the New York City Council and funding from the federal government. Once completed, Runway Green’s facility will serve up to 50,000 New York City public school students per year, according to the organization. “Runway Green will equip New York City students with the skills and experiences they need to succeed while making one of Brooklyn’s great public assets more accessible, engaging and meaningful to the communities it serves,” U.S. Sen. Charles Schumer said in a statement. bullets: Runway Green nonprofit signs 60-year lease for 7 acres at Floyd Bennett Field, Brooklyn Marine Park; $60M education campus.
Phase 1 breaks ground next year; 3 acres dedicated to urban farming with Campaign Against Hunger partnership; workforce development focus.
Long-term anchor use (60-year NPS lease) removes land from residential/commercial development in high-demand Brooklyn marine gateway area.
stories.summary: Runway Green, a workforce development nonprofit, signed a 60-year ground lease with the National Park Service for 7 acres at Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn's Marine Park neighborhood to develop a $60 million agricultural and environmental education facility. Phase 1 will begin next year and dedicate 3 acres to urban farming in partnership with Campaign Against Hunger. The project targets young people and aims to create a learning ecosystem connecting schools, employers, nonprofits, colleges, and public agencies.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. However, this removes 7 developable acres from the Brooklyn residential pipeline in a peripheral but increasingly gentrifying waterfront area; any future residential upside on Gateway NRA land is now off-market long-term. Developers active in outer-borough Brooklyn should note that NPS/federal land-use agreements can lock out decades of mixed-use/residential opportunities.

stories.title: European Coworking Firm Enters U.S. With 32K-SF Lease in Downtown L.A.
stories.excerpt: European flexible workspace operator InfinitSpace is entering the U.S. market with a 32,000-square-foot location in Downtown Los Angeles, its first step in a plan to open 30 locations nationwide in the next two years. The company announced Tuesday that it has entered into a long-term management partnership at the historic Desmond’s Building at 612 South Broadway. The new coworking spot, operating under infinitSpace’s Beyond brand, is scheduled to open Nov. 2. The workspace will occupy the second through fifth floors of the building, accommodating approximately 400 memberships with private offices, shared workspaces, meeting rooms and lounges. It will also feature a rooftop event space. An option for the sixth floor could add another 8,500 square feet, for about 40,500 square feet total. Unlike traditional coworking operators that lease space directly from landlords, InfinitSpace uses an asset-light management model in which property owners retain ownership and long-term control of their buildings. The company handles workspace operations, sales, marketing and technology, including an artificial intelligence platform designed to automate administrative tasks. The Los Angeles opening will mark InfinitSpace’s 15th location worldwide. The company serves more than 8,000 members on three continents, and expects to reach approximately 10,000 members by year’s end. Its initial U.S. expansion will focus on Los Angeles, San Francisco, Austin, Seattle and New York. “Property owners are looking for ways to make their buildings more productive and responsive to how companies use space, while businesses want flexibility without compromising the quality of their workplace,” InfinitSpace CEO and co-founder Wybo Wijnbergen said in a statement. “Our partnership model and technology were built to address both needs.” The Desmond’s Building opened in 1924 in Downtown L.A.’s Broadway Theatre District as the flagship store of clothing retailer Desmond’s. bullets: InfinitSpace (European coworking) enters U.S. with 32K SF lease at 612 South Broadway, Downtown L.A.; plans 30 locations nationwide in 2 years.
Beyond-branded coworking opens Nov. 2; ~400 memberships; asset-light management model (owner retains title); option for 6th floor adds 8.5K SF.

stories.summary: European flexible workspace operator InfinitSpace is entering the U.S. market with a 32,000-square-foot location in Downtown Los Angeles under its Beyond brand at the historic Desmond's Building, with plans to open 30 locations nationwide within two years. The company announced a long-term management partnership in which the property owner retains ownership while InfinitSpace handles workspace operations, sales, and marketing. The L.A. location, opening November 2, will accommodate approximately 400 memberships with an option for an additional 8,500 square feet on the sixth floor.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, the expansion of asset-light coworking into secondary markets and distressed office signals continued office-to-flex conversion and demand for smaller, shorter-lease workplace footprints among younger/remote-hybrid workers. This keeps office vacancy high and conversion feasibility marginal, making office-to-residential conversion less likely in secondary downtowns unless rents collapse further. For L.A., this reinforces ongoing pressure on Downtown office fundamentals.

stories.title: Investor Daryl Hagler Takes Over Ridgewood’s Embattled Resi Tower Development
stories.excerpt: Real estate investor and controversial health care mogul Daryl Hagler has signed on the dotted line to take over one of the most embattled developments in Ridgewood, Queens. The under-construction mixed-use tower at 3-50 St. Nicholas Avenue changed hands Tuesday for $75.8 million in cash, according to city records, with entities tied to troubled developer Arch Companies and Meir Babaev’s AB Capstone conveying the development to Hagler’s CDK 3-50 St. Nicholas. Toronto-based investor Kevin Wiener, whose family office 35 Oak Holdings previously partnered with developers Arch and AB Capstone, signed for the seller entities. Spokespeople for Arch, Wiener and Capstone could not be immediately reached for comment. The 252,850-square-foot structure, bounded by Ridgewood’s Palmetto Street, Myrtle Avenue and Nicholas Avenue, is slated to host 133 residential units, as well as a large retail component. A Burlington location quietly opened its doors there this month, Grimes Square reported, but the apartments remain unoccupied. The site secured a certificate of occupancy in August, according to Department of Buildings records. The transaction on Tuesday left in place mortgages from Madison Realty Capital with outstanding amounts totaling $75 million, with Hagler’s CDK LLC assuming the debt obligations. Hagler also secured the 99-year ground lease for an accompanying parcel for $10.2 million, according to the filing. A spokesperson for Madison declined to comment. Jeffrey Simpson and Jared Chassen’s Arch Companies purchased a stake in the project from Babaev’s Capstone in 2021, according to Crain’s New York Business. Brothers Kevin and Michael Wiener also joined the project as investors. The project, most recently dubbed the Ridgewood, was mired in community pushback from its earliest days. bullets: Daryl Hagler (CDK Capital) acquires 3-50 St. Nicholas Ave, Ridgewood Queens for $75.8M in cash; takes over Arch/Capstone troubled project.
252.8K SF mixed-use tower; 133 residential units, large retail (Burlington opened); units remain unoccupied; under construction.
Distressed developer transition; cash buyout suggests previous lenders or equity holders capitulated; new operator must complete/lease-up in uncertain market.
stories.summary: Real estate investor Daryl Hagler, via CDK Capital, acquired the under-construction mixed-use tower at 3-50 St. Nicholas Avenue in Ridgewood, Queens, for $75.8 million in cash from troubled developers Arch Companies and AB Capstone (seller entities tied to Kevin Wiener/35 Oak Holdings). The 252,850-square-foot project includes 133 residential units and substantial retail space; a Burlington location opened this month, but apartments remain unoccupied. The property is bounded by Palmetto Street, Myrtle Avenue, and Nicholas Avenue.
stories.impact: Hagler's all-cash acquisition of a stalled, under-occupied mixed-use tower signals distressed conditions in Ridgewood development market and willingness of motivated buyers to pay below replacement cost. For multifamily developers, this illustrates execution and lease-up risk in outer-borough Queens; Hagler's operational playbook (likely repositioning, aggressive marketing, possible rate cuts) will compete with any new ground-up or repositioning plays in Ridgewood. Watch for lease-up timeline and rental absorption; if units remain unoccupied, it signals weak underlying demand or pricing in that submarket.

stories.title: EliseAI, Manhattan-Based Proptech Unicorn, Raises $350M
stories.excerpt: EliseAI, an artificial intelligence company automating housing and health care systems, announced Tuesday that it has raised $350 million, bringing the proptech unicorn’s valuation to $4 billion. Andreessen Horowitz (also known as a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with participation from the Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures and Navitas Capital. EliseAI will use the capital to accelerate the development and delivery of new products, automating more of its customers’ operations, and to grow its engineering, deployment and sales teams across its North American offices. Additionally, it plans to establish San Francisco as a second engineering hub alongside its Manhattan headquarters. “Our customers ask us to support more of their operations every year, and we raised now so we can keep pace with that demand,” Minna Song, co-founder and CEO of EliseAI, told Commercial Observer. “We’re investing in a second engineering hub in San Francisco alongside New York, and we’re hiring across engineering, deployment, and sales in New York, Boston, Chicago, Austin and Toronto. We’re investing in building a product that handles the daily work of running a building: leasing, renewals, maintenance, collections and the questions residents send at all hours.” EliseAI bills itself as the only AI product in the space to work with all property types, from conventional multifamily to scattered-site and single-family properties to student and affordable properties, as well as properties managed locally and through centralization. In June 2026, EliseAI announced that it had surpassed $200 million in annual recurring revenue, doubling revenue year-over-year for five consecutive years. The platform now powers one in six U.S. apartments, and more than 30 million Americans have interacted with EliseAI since its founding, according to the company. bullets: EliseAI (Manhattan proptech unicorn) raises $350M Series C; valuation $4B; a16z and Bessemer led; Ontario Teachers, Sapphire, Navitas participated.
Capital to accelerate product development, automate customer operations, and build second engineering hub in San Francisco alongside NYC HQ.
Hiring across engineering, deployment, sales in New York, Boston, Chicago, Austin; AI automation of housing and health care systems.
stories.summary: EliseAI, an artificial intelligence company automating housing and health care systems, announced a $350 million Series C funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Venture Partners, bringing its valuation to $4 billion. The capital will accelerate product development, automate customer operations, and grow its engineering, deployment, and sales teams across North American offices. EliseAI plans to establish San Francisco as a second engineering hub alongside its Manhattan headquarters and expand hiring across New York, Boston, Chicago, and Austin.
stories.impact: EliseAI's $350M funding and $4B valuation validate the proptech/multifamily automation market; the company's growth in Boston, Chicago, and Austin signals those metros are hubs for multifamily-focused AI deployment and customer concentration. For Trammell Crow and peer developers, this highlights operational efficiency tooling (tenant screening, lease management, revenue optimization) becoming table-stakes competitive assets; vendors with strong product-market fit in multifamily are well-capitalized and will intensify competition for enterprise software wallet share. Developers should evaluate EliseAI and similar platforms for operational leverage on new communities.
